discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics - two-dimensional quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that rotating two graphene layers by a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees collapses the electronic bandwidth, producing nearly flat moire bands where interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realised this experimentally with tear-and-stack fabrication, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in a single, gate-tunable carbon device. This established the twist angle as a new control knob for quantum matter. It launched the field of moire materials, which has since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Chern insulators and, in twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states at zero magnetic field. Laboratories worldwide, including mine, now use van der Waals twist engineering to design strongly correlated and topological phases on demand. Few experiments in the past two decades have changed so completely how condensed-matter physicists create and study emergent electronic phenomena.
